If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 1–2% in the early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 1–2% in the mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract downward momentum.

If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 3–5% in the late horizon (16–30 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast in early horizon to capture momentum.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast in mid horizon to avoid false support.

If sentiment is consistently bearish over 5+ days, apply a 2–4% downward bias across all horizons to reflect structural risk.
